parole.testo: Inherited from Middle French dauve, from Old French dolve, from Late Latin dolva, related to the name of a buttercup that grows in swamps, attested in the fifth century and possibly of Celtic origin.

From Old French freperie, feuperie (“old clothes, rags”), from frepe, feupe (“clothes, rags”), from Late Latin faluppa (“straw, fiber, chip”), which is possibly a loan from Celtic. By surface analysis, fripe + -erie.
From Late Latin glenare, a Celtic borrowing from Gaulish, possibly from Proto-Celtic *glanos.

parole.significato: hem, border of a plate or cup
parole.testo: Inherited from Old French soue (“rope”) + -age, from Late Latin, Vulgar Latin soca, of Celtic origin, from Gaulish *soucā, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *sew- (“to bend, to cut, to drive”), see also Sanskrit सुवति (suvati).

Inherited from Late Latin troia. Cognate with Italian troia, Occitan truèja, Catalan truja, Walloon troye.
